Static secrets: long-lived, shared, and not tied to a user
The /legacy API only, sent as the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header.
None. An opaque string: no user, no roles, no expiry.
The Foundry connection mcp-legacy-key (custom keys), and anyone who copies it.
APIM only, plus a rate limit of 120 calls a minute per subscription key (else per

The deployment creates it as the Key Vault secret vendor-api-key.
The simulated market-data vendor, a third party outside the private network.
None. An opaque string sent as the x-vendor-key header.
Key Vault (APIM reads it as a named value) plus a plain Container Apps secret
copy on the vendor app. The user and the agent never see it.
The vendor (401 invalid_vendor_key). APIM adds it only after validating the user's
token, and removes the user's Authorization header.
Entra ID: a client secret on the confidential app registration abw-agent-client.
Entra's token endpoint, when Foundry exchanges a user's consent code for T2.
80 days. Setup-Entra.ps1 creates a new one when fewer than 10 days remain.
The Foundry OAuth connections and the git-ignored .secrets folder.
- Four tokens do the work: T1 gets a person into Foundry, T2 carries the person through the gateway and the MCP server, T3 is the server's own identity, and T4 reaches data as that
- Every token names its audience. T2 for one server fails at the others, and T4 works only at the one data service it was issued for.
- The static secrets (C3, C5, C6) are long-lived, shared and carry no user. The four data-backed MCP servers hold none of them: they use managed identities.
